title: MemeGuard: An LLM and VLM-based Framework for Advancing Content Moderation via Meme Intervention
measurement_description: The paper primarily measures the performance of Large Language Models (LLMs) and Vision Language Models (VLMs) in understanding toxic and cyberbullying memes and generating contextually appropriate natural language interventions. Religion is evaluated as one of several specific sub-categories of 'toxic elements' and societal biases that models are expected to identify and mitigate when countering cyberbullying content.
findings: The paper does not provide specific quantitative findings isolated to religious bias or theological knowledge. However, it incorporates religion as a core category of toxicity to be mitigated in memes. Through topic modeling of the generated interventions, the study found that models like FLAN-T5 successfully generated text addressing religious topics (specifically extracting topics mentioning 'Muslims' and 'Saudi') when countering cyberbullying memes. Overall, the proposed MemeGuard framework effectively generates appropriate interventions against various biases, which broadly include religious hostility.
